observations.behavior: Adds a new tool definition entry, "logs-group-by", with a detailed description and usage examples.
observations.code_quote:
"description": "Count logs grouped by up to 4 dimensions in one call. All parameters go inside `query`:

```json
{ "query": { "dateRange": { "date_from": "-24h" }, "groupBys": [{ "key": "pattern", "source": "column" }] } }
```

Each group has `values` (one per dimension, in request order), `log_count`, `error_count`, `first_seen` and `last_seen`. `truncated` is true when more groups matched than `limit`.

Use it instead of SQL for "top errors by service", "which patterns fail most" or "which sessions are noisiest". Use `logs-services-create` for a per-service health summary against a baseline, `logs-patterns-diff` for new or growing patterns, and `query-logs` to read the rows of one group.

Dimensions in `groupBys`:

- `source: "column"`: `service_name`, `severity_level`, `pattern` (the masked message template), `trace_id`, `span_id`.
- `source: "log"`: a log attribute key, for example `session_id`.
- `source: "resource"`: a resource attribute key, for example `k8s.pod.name`.

Rows without a value for a dimension are not counted. `orderGroupsBy` is `log_count`, `error_count` or `last_seen` (descending). Filter with `severityLevels`, `serviceNames`, `searchTerm` and `filterGroup`. Results are cached for 60 seconds.",
observations.posthog_connection: Adds documentation and metadata for a new MCP tool, "Group logs by attributes", which could help users query logs grouped by dimensions. No implementation or tests are shown.

observations.behavior: Updates the description and metadata for the "logs-services-create" tool, changing its purpose and parameters.
observations.code_quote:
"description": "List every service that logged in the window, with its health against a baseline. All other parameters go inside `query`:

```json
{ "query": { "dateRange": { "date_from": "-24h" }, "compare": "previous_day", "environment": "production" } }
```

Each row has `log_count`, `error_count`, `error_rate_pct` and `last_seen`. With `compare`, each row also gets a `status` and a short `reason`.
The status is `ok`, `degraded` (5% errors or more), `regressed` or `improved` (error rate up or down by 1 pp and 2x), `recovered`, `new` (no baseline logs) or `silent` (baseline logs, none now).
Silent services appear only with a baseline.
This is the entry point for "which services are silent, new or worse".
Use `logs-group-by` for counts by pattern or attribute, `logs-patterns-diff` for the error patterns behind a regression, and `logs-count-ranges` for when a spike started.

`compare` is `none` (default), `previous_period`, `previous_day` or `previous_week`. `baselineDateRange`, next to `query`, sets an explicit baseline.
`environment` matches the first set resource attribute of `deployment.environment.name`, `deployment.environment` and `env`.
`window` gives the absolute UTC bounds. `next` holds prefilled follow-up calls. It is empty when `environment` is set, because those tools do not filter by environment.",
observations.posthog_connection: Updates documentation and metadata for the "List services with health status" tool, potentially changing its behavior and parameters. No implementation or tests are shown.
